task_text: Peg In Hole: The hovering aerial manipulator starts holding a metal peg (a cylinder 15 cm long and 4 cm in diameter) in its gripper, pointing straight ahead. A wall stands ahead with a blue square socket mounted on its front face: a square frame whose square opening faces the robot and is closed at the back by a red plate. Insert the peg: the centre of the peg's front end (the end pointing ahead at the start) must be inside the square opening and more than 2 cm deep into it (the opening is 3 cm deep up to the red plate). Success: Success at a control step when the peg tip p = peg root position + R(peg) (0.075, 0, 0) (the centre of the end face that points ahead at reset), expressed in the socket's frame as q = R(socket)^T (p - socket root position), satisfies q.x > 0 (peg_insertion_depth_min = 0: past the socket's mid-plane, i.e. more than 0.02 m behind its front face; the red plate's surface is at q.x = 0.01), |q.y| < 0.03 s and |q.z| < 0.03 s (half the scaled opening side 0.06 s); all inequalities strict. Only this point is tested: the peg's orientation, whether it is still held and contacts are not checked. AM-Bench reports no subtask criteria for this task. Evaluated after every control step (decimation 1, so after every 1/120 s physics step) on the simulated state; no hold time is required. The episode terminates at the first step where it holds. Otherwise it is truncated by the time limit: episode_length_s = 20 s, i.e. max_episode_length = 2400 control steps; AM-Bench raises the time-out when episode_length_buf >= max_episode_length - 1, i.e. at the 2399th step.
episode: one episode, no reset: it ends at the first control step where AM-Bench's success check holds, when the task's episode length of 20 s of simulated time runs out (AM-Bench's time-out, at control step 2399), when your time is up, or on a simulator error; the simulated clock advances only with the control steps you run
